notes: Same access route (direct HTTP fetch, SSR __NEXT_DATA__ decode, no block). Found a genuine top-level header mega-menu item 'New Arrivals' (url /department/newarrivals) with 12 real department children, each pointing to that department's category page filtered by the site's own 'NEW' product badge (q=badge.title.en:NEW). Opened /department/newarrivals itself first: it is a static CMS landing page (staticPageReducer, no own nbHits/product grid) that just shows tiles linking to the 12 department pages, so it fails the 'products actually listed' test and is NOT recorded as its own row - only the 12 department PLPs beneath it were evaluated individually by opening each and reading the exact nbHits the storefront's own Algolia-backed search response (algoliaCategoryReducer.searchData.nbHits, which matches the rendered product-count header) reports for that badge=NEW filter. 11 of the 12 department listings are genuine, verifiably filtered subsets (each much smaller than that department's unfiltered total, e.g. Decor NEW=223 vs unfiltered household-decor=1335+; Baby & Kids NEW=582 vs unfiltered babyandkids=3342) and were included below. The 12th, Fragrances, uses a different URL pattern (q=:index:recent-products, a SORT order not a badge filter) and returned nbHits=848 - identical to the unfiltered household-homefragrance category total of 848 - proving it is the entire Fragrances catalog merely re-sorted by recency, not an actual 'newly added' subset; it was excluded as not genuinely representing new arrivals. Also found a second, footer-nav 'New Arrivals' link set with a different query format (badge.title.en:New title-case, plus an appended :index:recent-products) pointing to the same 12 departments; tested it (Furniture, Lighting) and it returns nbHits=0 for every department - a broken/stale query string, not a genuine alternate listing - so it was discarded in favor of the working header-nav (uppercase NEW) URLs, which are recorded below as canonical. Checked sitemap_categories.xml and internal search ('new arrivals' -> nbHits=2000, a non-discriminating fallback count) as supporting checks only; the mega-menu discovery above is the ground truth. Checked for Arabic-locale equivalents: the nav tree is locale-shared (same node IDs, only the label text differs between en/ar), so no separate Arabic-only New Arrivals structure exists beyond what's captured here.
